timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Good morning everybody. We are camping in Usury Mountain Regional Park in Mesa, Arizona.
And I just wanted to kind of show you around a little bit. It is gorgeous out here.
We love this campsite. It's clean. There's about 70, I think, 78 camp spots out here.
One that we have, turning around a little bit. This is our campsite here. This one is a pull-through.
They have back ends also. And I like this so. I like this one a lot.
Very scenic. Have I mentioned how beautiful I think this is?
The spots are not right on top of each other, which is really nice.
We didn't hear any neighbors or anything. It was super quiet at night. Right out this way, we could see the lights of Mesa.
And then over the other way over here a little bit, you could see the lights of Phoenix.
So that was really, really neat to watch. Right up there is the Winke trail.
You look like you want to try that.
I don't know. There is nothing in here that wants to try that.
You sure?
On the side of the hill over here is Phoenix. And an arrow pointing towards Phoenix.
Now those are my kind of directional signs. One of the things I was going to mention is we have water and electricity.
There is a dump station in the campground. So as we leave, we'll use the dump station.
The hookups are over there. And we had to go all the way from this side over here to hook up.
So Bob knew that ahead of time. And he brought extra long hoses and cords so that he could hook up all the way over here.
So just keep that in mind. You might want to bring longer hoses and cords.
Camp sites are on level. So make sure you bring blocks.
We noticed a lot of the RVs had their wheels up off the ground, actually.
But once you got level, everything was good.
Bob has some thoughts on the campground too. So I'm going to hand it over to Bob and let him say a few words.
Hi there. We're at Usury Regional Mountain Park. Mountain Regional Park, something like that.
And this has some of the nicest individual camp spots for a desert park that we have been to.
And we've been to a lot of desert parks from Death Valley, Burnus Creek, Shashone, Bady, Courtside, Yuma, just to name a few.
This has got some of the best individual camp spots we've seen.
You know, a hole in the wall was pretty nice in Mojave National Preserve.
But this has got some really nice ones. The thing is, it's not a destination like some of those other places.
You know, Death Valley, Bady, all those places have a million things to do in list.
This only has a couple things to do. So just for info, really nice place to camp and we've really enjoyed it.
It's hard to get a spot here if you try and get a spot and they say that they're booked up, keep trying.
Because sometimes they have cancellations and you can get a spot when there's a cancellation, especially if you're flexible.
And you know, you're not set on certain dates or certain days of the week.
We're going to take off for the day and go see what kind of trouble we can get into.
So I'll talk to you guys later. Bye.

#221 #UseryMountainRegionalPark #RVLife #nosmallcreator

Camping Usery Mountain Regional Park. We spent the last couple of days at Usery Mountain Regional Park. It was so beautiful, we had to share it with you. For more information on the park, here's a link to their website:
https://www.maricopacountyparks.net/park-locator/usery-mountain-regional-park/
There's so many things to do in the area. We spent a whole day exploring. We went to the Superstition Mountains Museum, Lost Dutchman State Park and had lunch in the Ghost Town of Goldfield Arizona. We plan on coming back!

Follow me on Facebook - Ramblin Pam

All photos and video were shot with my Samsung Galaxy cellphone - nothing fancy.
